newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel seeks FY98 $209 mln SPR oil sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel seeks FY98 $209 mln SPR oil sale.

text.p: The U.S. House Interior Appropriations subcommittee Tuesday proposed a $209 million sale of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for the 1998 fiscal year.
Panel Chairman Ralph Regula, an Ohio Republican, said the money was needed to cover the cost of running the oil reserve.

The Energy Department had announced that the administration had pulled from its five-year budget plan a proposed sale for $1.15 billion of SPR oil in fiscal 2002, saying it wanted to avoid sales that depleted the reserve.
House Commerce Committee Chairman Thomas Bliley, a Virginia Republican, last week wrote to Appropriations Committee leaders urging them to drop the proposed 1998 sale.
